entries.text: The claim on the table is that writing will nearly vanish as a common skill, and it rests on writing's difficulty being irreducible rather than incidental.
If the difficulty is permanent, only the countervailing pressure ever forced people through it, so what matters now is what happens when that pressure lifts.

A world of writes and write-nots would be harmless if writing were merely a craft, so the cost of the split turns on writing being thinking — and once that is granted, the only thing left undecided is who chooses to remain smart.
